AAS (IDTA Parts 1–5 and selected templates; bounded partial)
01 — IDENTITY & DESCRIPTION — Identify a manufacturer, reusable model, particular unit and API identity without collapsing them.

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: ManufacturerName explicitly identifies the product producer; the TechnicalData use case can also treat a supplier as manufacturer. Retain a common manufacturer-information candidate, distinct from operator and instance identity. [Sources: AAS09-N014, AAS09-N015; F3-05-S06-R001]

RELATED: BSI §6.2.5.15/Table32 declares ConfigurationData.manufacturer for the SAPIENT Node/interface component; not independently verified manufacturer of all installed physical instruments. [SAP03A-N12]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: Manufacturer identifies a component manufacturer, producer or vendor. The potential need to name the producer is common even when the native subject is a component; neither operator nor installed-unit provenance is established. [ISA21:S06-R001; F3-02]

RELATED: C239 §6.3 replaceable-unit (FRU) inventory, §8.3 MORA getManufacturer, and PIC Certificate of Volatility identify vendor in specific contexts, not a verified fielded-unit manufacturer. The 2022 v1 DSDM models Manufacturer–Product links [G3-N2]; original C239 2023 native byte equivalence remains unverified. [G2-3/G2-4B/G2-6A/G3-N2]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: ManufacturerProductDesignation, article number and order code support qualified product/model identification. Product designation text is not automatically a reusable model identifier; AssetKind and template kind remain different concepts. [Sources: AAS09-N015, AAS02-N011; F3-05-S06-R002]
RELATED: BSI §6.2.5.15/Table32 ConfigurationData.model names the Node product, not a guaranteed model identifier for the whole installation or every physical subcomponent. [SAP03A-N12]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] DIRECT: Model identifies the component model within its manufacturer product line. Product model designation is a reusable information need; this is a product kind, not an individual unit. [ISA21:S06-R002; F3-02]

RELATED/PARTIAL: C239 §5.3 Procurable Unit, §6.3 FRU model, RF getModel/getEquipmentId, and PIC documentation use different product/part/instance scopes. None proves a model of an installed whole System. The 2022 DSDM distinguishes Product and ProductInstance but Product.name need not be a model number; C239 native equivalence unverified. [SOSA-D/G2-3/G2-4B/G2-6A/G3-N2]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: SpecificAssetId and AssetLink can carry a named serial number or other scoped asset identifier. Retain a common individual-identity candidate without equating serial, globalAssetId, product number or a verified installed unit. [Sources: AAS02-N012, AAS02-N009, AAS06-N006; F3-05-S06-R003]
PARTIAL: BSI Table32 serial_number is conditional for hardware Nodes; pure-software Nodes may use product/license numbers. Not every Node serial is a physical equipment serial. [SAP03A-N12]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: Serial Number identifies a component within its manufacturer/model; the combined manufacturer/model/serial is expected to be globally unique. A manufacturer-scoped serial is useful across equipment types, but the source does not verify a serial-numbered physical probe in any case. [ISA21:S06-R003; F3-02]

RELATED: C239 §6.3 FRU inventory includes serial number but proves no installed case-equipment serial. NO_ESTABLISHED: an orderable fixed-pin-variant part number is not an individual serial number. [G2-3; G2-7Q §13.5.4.2.6.2]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: AAS Identifiable.id and represented-asset identifiers support distinct persistent identity roles. Preserve shell versus asset identity, scoped idShort and unprotected asset binding; neither an identifier nor an authenticated API proves the physical System identity. [Sources: AAS02-N018, AAS02-N009, AAS08-N042; F3-05-S06-R004]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] RELATED: BSI §6.2.4 uses the same Node UUID across subsequent messages. This supports qualified persistent source identity; the timestamp conflict does not invalidate UUID meaning. Physical equipment identity and lifetime persistence are not established. [SAP02-N03, SAP03A-N03]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: UCI is the string used persistently to refer to a specific ISA component; virtual components use qualified identifiers. Persistent component identity is a common need. Preserve ICD syntax/certificate association and CMPT virtual suffix rules as source constraints, not universal DIM rules. [ISA21:S06-R004; F3-02]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: Sensor.elementID supports qualified sensing-entity identification. Its 2022 integer identifier has no established globally persistent URI or lifetime guarantee; those identity constraints remain held. A useful identifier candidate does not require exact ISA or OGC identity semantics. 2022 lineage; exact 2023 companion bytes unverified. [F3-04A-S06-R004]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: Part 4 defines issuer-key trust, signed access tokens and dataspace trust policy; public certificates are one permitted key source. This supports qualified trust-context information. Device certificate binding is only a possible approach, not a required equipment certificate or an authenticated physical identity. [Sources: AAS08-N033, AAS08-N041, AAS08-N042; F3-05-ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST]
Not assessed here — no verified SAPIENT correspondence is recorded for this topic; not evidence that the donor lacks it.

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: The ICD requires a valid certificate signed by a valid certification authority within the network PKI. This supports common identity/trust context while retaining native certificate-name, validity, revocation and algorithm qualifications from the prior corpus; no installed certificate is verified. [ICD-3.1.2, ICD-3.3, ICD-6.1, CERT-1.0, CERT-2.0, CERT-3.1, CERT-3.2, CERT-3.2.1, CERT-3.2.2, CERT-3.3, CERT-3.4; F3-06-ISA-ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST]

RELATED: C239 §6.5.4 root-of-trust, §12 security/key/digest obligations, and conditional §15 inter-module TLS/DTLS concern trust and protection; §14 container permissions remain unspecified. No mandatory ISA certificate Common Name, issuer/trust-anchor schema, or actual installed certificate is established. [G2-3/G2-5/G2-7R/G2-7S] SO-2D: root-of-trust may be hardware/software and cryptographic or design-based. The secure-startup authentication dependencies are preserved separately in SOSA-SO2D-SECURE-STARTUP; neither a certificate schema nor a successful authentication follows.
02 — SYSTEM, EQUIPMENT & RELATIONSHIPS — Describe the whole, physical constituents, separate connections, reporting participant and hosting context.

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: A shell describes an asset through informational submodels; assets can include physical equipment and software. Retain a qualified described-system candidate while separating the represented asset, digital shell, design/type/instance context and actual sensing installation. [Sources: AAS02-N002, AAS03-N001, AAS09-N001; F3-05-S06-R005]

RELATED: BSI Annex C describes an optional separately registered middleware Node participating in a SAPIENT network; neither the middleware nor the detected-object taxonomy defines one physical whole sensing assembly. [SAP06-N14,SAP06-N19]

[SPECIALIZED CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: A Composition Interface Component (CIC) exposes a composition of members through an ISA interface. The optional architecture-specific integration arrangement is useful specialized information; it does not establish one physical assembly or a universal root. [ISA21:S06-R005; F3-02]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] NARROWER/PARTIAL: C239 explicitly describes a sensing system containing one or more physical hardware elements, potentially spanning several modalities. This supports the common need to describe the sensing arrangement. Optional cards, chassis and software profiles do not erase that meaning or establish a universal DIM root or installed configuration. [F3-04A-S06-R005]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: Descriptors and endpoints identify API network resources and offered interfaces. They support common network-participant description on the same basis as logical ISA and SOSA participants; preserve optional shell endpoints, asset-versus-shell identity and unverified reachability. [AAS06-N003, AAS06-N004; F3-06-AAS-S06-R006]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] RELATED: A SAPIENT Node is an identified architecture participant; optional middleware can also register as a Node. Useful network-participant identity does not require a one-to-one correspondence with physical sensing hardware. [SAP02-N02, SAP02-N03, SAP03A-N03, SAP03A-N04, SAP06-N14]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: An ISA component or Controller is an interface-conformant network participant or service role. Describing the participant role is a common need; neither a physical sensor nor the original observation performer follows from network visibility. [ISA21:S06-R006; F3-02]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] RELATED: C239 names interaction endpoints implemented by modules or hardware elements. These support describing a network participant independently of physical equipment identity. The modeled endpoint is not proof of live discovery, an independently exposed CSAPI System or an installed service. [F3-04A-S06-R006]
Not assessed here — no AAS comparison established from the reviewed source; not evidence of absence.

F3_02_ISA_classification.native_subject_and_meaning: UCI is the string used persistently to refer to a specific ISA component; virtual components use qualified identifiers.
F3_02_ISA_classification.rationale: Persistent component identity is a common need. Preserve ICD syntax/certificate association and CMPT virtual suffix rules as source constraints, not universal DIM rules.
F3_02_ISA_classification.peer_difference: Like other donor identifiers, identity can be common without equating ISA component UCI to a physical unit, AAS asset ID or CSAPI System URI.

F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.rationale: BSI §6.2.4 uses the same Node UUID across subsequent messages. This supports qualified persistent source identity; the timestamp conflict does not invalidate UUID meaning. Physical equipment identity and lifetime persistence are not established.
F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.native_preservation: Original native findings and all historical correspondence records retained; target claims, performance, fusion role, alert lifecycle and detection-lineage candidates remain separately represented.
F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.peer_criterion: Grade useful information at its source subject; do not require exact ISA/OGC equivalence or observed installed equipment. A different subject or unsupported relationship remains held. Requiredness and runtime validity are separate.

F3_04A_OpenGroupSOSA_classification.rationale: Sensor.elementID supports qualified sensing-entity identification. Its 2022 integer identifier has no established globally persistent URI or lifetime guarantee; those identity constraints remain held. A useful identifier candidate does not require exact ISA or OGC identity semantics.

F3_05_AAS_classification.rationale: AAS Identifiable.id and represented-asset identifiers support distinct persistent identity roles. Preserve shell versus asset identity, scoped idShort and unprotected asset binding; neither an identifier nor an authenticated API proves the physical System identity.

No mandatory ISA certificate Common Name, issuer/trust-anchor schema, or actual installed certificate is established. [G2-3/G2-5/G2-7R/G2-7S] SO-2D: root-of-trust may be hardware/software and cryptographic or design-based. The secure-startup authentication dependencies are preserved separately in SOSA-SO2D-SECURE-STARTUP; neither a certificate schema nor a successful authentication follows.
rows.boundary: ICD6.0r5 requires a valid certificate under the network PKI and checks the Controller certificate Common Name against its UCI. The Certificate Guide distinguishes SDK,local testing,exercise and deployment certificates; deployment follows the deploying authority policy. This establishes source requirements,not installed credentials,verified trust,physical identity,permission for a task or current security certification. Virtual-component UCI suffixes do not imply a separate certificate for every virtual member. CMPT §4.1.2 separately requires date validity and nonrevocation. Its high/mid and low-level signer clauses respectively say ISA-approved and acceptable to the deploying organization. M-0004/L-0011 say ECDSA, while L-0013 is titled ECDSA Algorithm but says ECDH; L-0012 literally says the certificate is at least 384 bits long. These statements remain attributed without a repaired algorithm, inferred key-size field or current cryptographic recommendation. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller registration compares the REQUEST ADD originating UCI with the certificate UCI before authorization. Certificate matching does not prove physical identity, completed certificate trust validation or permission to join.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller registration compares the REQUEST ADD originating UCI with the certificate UCI before authorization. Certificate matching does not prove physical identity, completed certificate trust validation or permission to join.

F3_02_ISA_classification.native_subject_and_meaning: An ISA component or Controller is an interface-conformant network participant or service role.
F3_02_ISA_classification.architecture_standing: SDD architecture description / optional integration approach; no DIM requirement
F3_02_ISA_classification.rationale: Describing the participant role is a common need; neither a physical sensor nor the original observation performer follows from network visibility.
F3_02_ISA_classification.peer_difference: AAS digital representation, SAPIENT Node and SOSA role must each retain their native subjects; blue is potential usefulness, not physical equivalence.
F3_02_ISA_classification.negative_equivalence_boundary: A visible network participant or Controller is not by definition a distinct physical sensor, installed device or original observation performer.

F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.rationale: A SAPIENT Node is an identified architecture participant; optional middleware can also register as a Node. Useful network-participant identity does not require a one-to-one correspondence with physical sensing hardware.
F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.native_preservation: Original native findings and all historical correspondence records retained; target claims, performance, fusion role, alert lifecycle and detection-lineage candidates remain separately represented.
F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.peer_criterion: Grade useful information at its source subject; do not require exact ISA/OGC equivalence or observed installed equipment. A different subject or unsupported relationship remains held. Requiredness and runtime validity are separate.

F3_04A_OpenGroupSOSA_classification.rationale: C239 names interaction endpoints implemented by modules or hardware elements. These support describing a network participant independently of physical equipment identity. The modeled endpoint is not proof of live discovery, an independently exposed CSAPI System or an installed service.

F3_05_AAS_classification.rationale: Descriptors identify API network resources and their offered interfaces. Retain a specialized service-participant candidate; the software endpoint is not automatically the described physical sensor or a demonstrated reachable device.

F3_06_AAS_classification.rationale: Descriptors and endpoints identify API network resources and offered interfaces. They support common network-participant description on the same basis as logical ISA and SOSA participants; preserve optional shell endpoints, asset-versus-shell identity and unverified reachability.

rows.boundary: The initiator is the client and the non-initiator is the server for that connection. Controller is a service responsibility and software role; it also has client-side responsibilities. These are not disjoint equipment classes, physical device counts or process counts. A visible network participant need not equal one physical device. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller discovery and incoming/outgoing secure network roles include Zeroconf and TCP/SCTP/Mockets in this source revision; no tested live topology or physical participant count follows.

rows.label: Composition member exposure and source attribution
rows.definition: A composition interface component (CIC) exposes composition and member capabilities and determines whether the network sees a member as their source or sees the CIC as their provider.
display: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: The hierarchy template explicitly indexes component assets and their own shells across distributed systems, enabling access to constituent data. This supports qualified member exposure/source attribution. Descriptor submodels alone are informational aspects, not physical members, and producer authenticity remains unverified. [Sources: AAS09-N001, AAS09-N002, AAS06-N003; F3-05-ISA-A-MEMBER-EXPOSURE]
Not assessed here — no verified SAPIENT correspondence is recorded for this topic; not evidence that the donor lacks it.

[SPECIALIZED CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: The CIC can expose a visible member with source attribution or make a member opaque and present its capabilities as CIC-provided. This is an optional mediation architecture, not physical part-of or a common requirement to hide members. [SDD-1.2, SDD-4.2.2, SDD-6.3.3; F3-06-ISA-ISA-A-MEMBER-EXPOSURE]

[SPECIALIZED CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/NO_ESTABLISHED: The 2022 SensorComponent_Info record exposes component IDs, names, types and in-band URIs associated with a Sensor. Preserve this optional component-description candidate. It does not establish an ISA visible/opaque policy, public child Systems, independent taskability or attribution of an observation to physical equipment. 2022 lineage; exact 2023 companion bytes unverified. [F3-04A-ISA-A-MEMBER-EXPOSURE]
Composition member exposure and source attribution
rows.boundary: Composition is an integration collection, not necessarily a physical assembly. A visible member is announced, has declared capabilities and periodic status; a non-ISA member made visible is a virtual ISA component. Opaque does not mean its capabilities are absent. This is network representation, not independently verified physical provenance or the DMS laser Visible property. CMPT §4.3.15 calls represented non-ISA-interface entities virtual ISA components and requires network announcements/configuration/status/observation handling on their behalf. This strengthens the network-representation interpretation, not physical part-of, independent certificate ownership or direct ISA connectivity. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: When an announcer deregisters or loses connection, still-announced members receive DEVICE REMOVED network notices; this does not prove they were physically disconnected or destroyed.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: When an announcer deregisters or loses connection, still-announced members receive DEVICE REMOVED network notices; this does not prove they were physically disconnected or destroyed.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: DEVICE REMOVED leads Live Data to discard retained Config/Status information for the cited participant; that is a service-visible state change, not proof of physical composition change or equipment destruction.

[HELD] NO_ESTABLISHED: C239 audit startup, shutdown and restart events describe the audit subsystem lifecycle. They do not establish connection-specific registration, configuration, operation and deregistration states. Keep this participation-lifecycle mapping held; retain the audit-event meaning. [F3-04A-ISA-A-PARTICIPATION-LIFECYCLE]
rows.boundary: The six phases describe ISA participation, not physical asset life, equipment health or command execution. Periodic Status supports communication availability; missing Status does not prove physical failure. Registration renewal, nonresponsive/revived handling, deregistration and connection termination remain distinct; a connection may remain open. Figures illustrate typical and atypical paths, not an invented complete implementation. CMPT distinguishes pre-operational integration, pre-participation discovery/time setup and participation behavior. Its client-side role is the connection initiator; startup connection need is conditional, and connection attempts are at least five seconds apart. M-0032/L-0083–0088 gate Request/Event/Administrative transmission and silently discard early arrivals until the connected peer’s initial Status is received. This initial-Status operational marker remains separately attributed from the SDD initial-Config transition. A permitted IPL data exchange is not automatic permission for every ISA message or proof of hardware readiness. CMPT §4.3.7 adds explicit NON RESPONSIVE and REVIVED recovery exchanges: selected Status within500ms and complete Config within30s. §4.3.16 separately requires resource cleanup and deregistration before leaving; connection termination remains source-qualified because M-0073 says should terminate after Registration Removed while L-0168 says the connection may close and may remain open. Recovery, deregistration and socket closure are not physical asset lifecycle states. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller-specific initial Config/Status deadlines, NON RESPONSIVE/REVIVED, forced REMOVED and mandatory forced connection termination are distinct actor/trigger rules; do not erase differing mid-/low-level time anchors or Component Requirements should/may socket wording.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller-specific initial Config/Status deadlines, NON RESPONSIVE/REVIVED, forced REMOVED and mandatory forced connection termination are distinct actor/trigger rules; do not erase differing mid-/low-level time anchors or Component Requirements should/may socket wording.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: DEVICE REMOVED causes Live Data maintained Config/Status cleanup and subscription consumer cleanup; network/cache lifecycle is distinct from physical hardware removal or historical observation deletion.

AAS04_IDTA01001_source_correspondence.meaning: Operation describes input, output and inoutput variables. It supports an interface comparison, while invocation, errors and execution contracts remain Part 2 work.

AAS10_owner_view_status.explanation: Qualified native comparison; prospective information only.

F3_04B_OpenGroupSOSA_classification.rationale: C239 names management request/response operations, including V1.0 updateMode and executeBIT, with scoped contracts. The 2022 UpdateMode request also declares its typed payload. This supports command-interface description without adopting one universal command catalogue, treating Future operations as current, or claiming execution.

F3_05_AAS_classification.rationale: Operation declares an invocable interface with input/output/inoutput variables; Part 2 defines synchronous and asynchronous invocation. Promote to common interface-declaration candidate. Physical effect and an exact ISA equipment-command catalogue remain unestablished.

F3_06_SAPIENT_classification.rationale: The pinned Task.Command schema declares named alternatives and their payload types. This supports qualified command-interface information under the same criterion as AAS and SOSA, without asserting a discoverable per-device command catalogue or physical execution.

AAS04_IDTA01001_source_correspondence.meaning: Part 1 declares an Operation and points to Part 2 invocation. A declaration is not an issued request; request identity, authorization and execution remain unreviewed here.

AAS10_owner_view_status.explanation: API invocation is not a verified physically issued control request.

F3_02_ISA_classification.native_subject_and_meaning: Request carries a command invocation, request identity and parameters, with access-control and expiry context.
F3_02_ISA_classification.rationale: Recording an issued control request is common; the message type or capability declaration alone does not prove an actual invocation, permission or hardware action.
F3_02_ISA_classification.peer_difference: AAS operation invocation and SAPIENT tasking may serve a common need while preserving separate request, authorization and execution semantics.
F3_02_ISA_classification.negative_equivalence_boundary: A type definition or capability declaration does not prove an actual issued Request, permission or performed/achieved hardware control.

F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.rationale: Task carries an identified control request to a Node. Native command/region specializations do not erase the general request information; acceptance, execution and physical effect remain distinct.
F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.native_preservation: Original native findings and all historical correspondence records retained; target claims, performance, fusion role, alert lifecycle and detection-lineage candidates remain separately represented.
F3_03_SAPIENT_classification.peer_criterion: Grade useful information at its source subject; do not require exact ISA/OGC equivalence or observed installed equipment. A different subject or unsupported relationship remains held. Requiredness and runtime validity are separate.

F3_04B_OpenGroupSOSA_classification.rationale: C239 V1.0 management requests and the 2022 typed UpdateMode request support describing a control request independently of exact ISA/CSAPI correspondence. Correct the earlier mixed hold to a qualified common candidate. Preliminary Task/Assignment interfaces remain separately qualified; no actual issued request, authorization or physical effect was verified.

F3_05_AAS_classification.rationale: Part 2 defines operation invocation requests and argument payloads. Promote to a common control-request interface candidate without requiring an observed device execution. An issued instance, authorization and physical effect remain unverified; a file-only capability description cannot execute a request.

SO2A_qualification.rationale: SO-2A: preserve externally originated Task versus internally originated Assignment, with target and source context; the task-interface publication limits remain.

SO2E_qualification.rationale: SO-2E: distinguish a command/request message from the identified task and its internal module assignments, retained in SOSA-SO2E-TASK-RECORD and SOSA-SO2E-TASK-ASSIGNMENT. Preliminary task-table standing does not establish implemented operations.

rows.label: Command acknowledgement / reported outcome
rows.definition: ACCEPTED is not COMPLETED, and COMPLETED is not measured physical effect.
display: [COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL/RELATED: The API separates receipt, execution state and reported business success. A 202 response can precede failure; HTTP 200 with executionState Failed reports invocation failure. Optional success separately describes the business operation. Neither transport success nor a reported result proves physical effect. Preserve the executionState prose/schema requiredness conflict. [Sources: AAS07-N008, AAS07-N010, AAS07-N011, AAS07-N012, AAS07-N052; O5-S06-R020]

PARTIAL: BSI TaskAck reports ACCEPTED/REJECTED/COMPLETED/FAILED and may repeat during a task; this is a reported disposition, not verified physical actuation or ISA Response schema. [SAP05-N11,SAP05-N12]

[COMMON CANDIDATE] PARTIAL: Response reports ongoing or final request disposition and result values. Acknowledgement/outcome reporting is common; queued/in-progress is not final success and a reported result is not independently verified physical effect. Authorization-service SUCCESS can accompany authorized=No. [ISA21:S06-R020; F3-02]

RELATED but not equivalent: C239 §7 Task Health and module request/response/error types can report task/command dispositions, but do not establish one ISA/CSAPI acknowledgement/result lifecycle or independently verify physical action. Some functions remain Future or reference-only. [SOSA-D/G2-2/G2-4B/G2-7S/T]

original_source_locators.source_meaning: Status/final request disposition and return values.
QUEUED/IN PROGRESS are nonfinal; SUCCESS is a final source-reported disposition.
Authorization determination SUCCESS with authorized Yes or No is distinct from command success.

source_first_correspondence.non_equivalence: Response code is a reported execution state not independent evidence of physical effect; even authorization denial can carry SUCCESS in its separate service context.

G2_2_source_correspondence.negative_equivalence_boundary: Object type in a source table does not prove completed command, fault-free response or ISA TaskAck equivalence.

rows.definition: A component message carrying optional capability declarations and separate ready/reporting state lists, with source-specified initial and update content rules.
display: Not assessed here — no AAS comparison established from the reviewed source; not evidence of absence.

RELATED: SAPIENT Registration contains declared Node capability/mode/status-report contracts and ConfigurationData manufacturer/model/versions; not the ISA Config message or validated installed hardware state. [SAP03A-N01,SAP03A-N12]

[HELD] RELATED_BUT_DIFFERENT: The 2022 Component characteristics and configuration responses describe health, mode, state and settings. They do not supply a report of capability declarations with separate per-capability ready/reporting selections. Keep this mapping held; current condition and configuration retrieval remain useful in their own rows. 2022 lineage; exact 2023 companion bytes unverified. [F3-04B-ISA-T-CONFIG] SO-2B: the reported user-modifiable settings set is retained separately in SOSA-SO2B-EQUIPMENT-SETTINGS; this capability/readiness correspondence remains held.
rows.boundary: Declarations and readiness/reporting states remain distinct from current Status values and performed work. ICD7.3 says a modifiable property is marked mutable in the CCD; clearing it makes it Not Ready,and not-ready properties must be Not Reporting and absent from Status. The DMS Clear Property precondition remains a value previously supplied through Set Property; its null-value consequence is retained. This does not establish deletion of historical data or physical absence. IPL3 declaration representations do not change the saved DMS declaration contracts. CMPT requires initial Config within 30 seconds of ADDED. L-0058 includes the CCD and all false capability-state values; L-0061 includes the entire CCD when declarations change; L-0062 includes all false state values when states change and explicitly describes an empty state list when all states become true. This is not an arbitrary sparse patch rule or a universal Boolean default. Updates retain the source’s all-connected-components versus connected-Controller wording. Configuration updates have a 30-second send limit. M-0031 separately requires property changes after configuration-set changes; L-0082 ties its full reporting-true Status to an update Config containing a CCD, and L-0170 gives that full Status a 30-second limit. These source levels do not establish a full-Status trigger for every state-only update. On REVIVED, CMPT requires a complete configuration set and a Config send within30 seconds of the revival notification. This is recovery traffic, not evidence that configuration was accepted, deployed or physically realized. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller initial Config mid-level received-first-Config and low-level outbound ADDED trigger wordings differ; updated Config carries only configuration-set changes, not Status property values.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller initial Config mid-level received-first-Config and low-level outbound ADDED trigger wordings differ; updated Config carries only configuration-set changes, not Status property values.

Separate Alert and STOP-reporting rules do not erase these fields or establish exact ISA Status equivalence. [SAP03A-N06, SAP03A-N08, SAP04-N01, SAP04-N02, SAP04-N07, SAP05-N06, SAP05-N13]

RELATED but different: C239 §6 Health, Status, State, Mode, diagnostics and SYSLOG plus §14 runtime settings distinguish conditions, setup and reported events; no universal ISA Status.properties name/value-message equivalence or measured case data. [SOSA-D/G2-1/2/G2-7R/T]
rows.boundary: Distinct from a Get Status request, Config states and Event observables. ICD 6.5 gives general Status publication bounds through Minimum/Maximum Status Interval and contextual significant change. The saved DMS Threshold Declaration also specifies threshold publication regardless of status interval; retain both source statements without inventing precedence. IPL3 encodes standard properties as optional typed fields and custom properties through the named-value structure; list presence is separate from list contents. The DMS Status.properties list remains unchanged. CMPT initial Status includes every ready-and-reporting property and is due within 30 seconds of sending initial Config. Periodic Status includes all and only changed ready-and-reporting property values; a never-reported value is treated as changed. L-0093’s 500 ms response is conditional on a reporting-true property change after no periodic Status within the Minimum Status Interval, not a universal period. L-0082’s CCD-update Status instead says every reporting-true property; preserve that qualification difference. The saved Get Status command separately retrieves declared ready properties even when reporting is disabled. M-0037’s explanatory Note says these interval restrictions apply only to Status publication; the ICD separately reuses the named interval properties for command-response cadence. CMPT non-responsiveness recovery uses a500ms Status response. Higher-level text says full status, while L-0100 explicitly selects declared properties with ready=true and reporting=true; retain that source-level wording difference instead of silently broadening the message to every declared property. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Initial Status mid-level and low-level triggers differ and have bounded timing; later Status carries changes only. Missed Status drives configurable network availability monitoring, not verified hardware failure.

It is not direct proof of physical health.

rows.boundary: Registration.credentials is application-message data; it is distinct from the TLS certificate required by the ICD connection rules and the Certificate Guide trust/usage context. The saved DMS fields specify no automatic registration success or particular credential scheme. Possessing a certificate does not by itself establish a permitted command,successful registration or verified deployment security. CMPT-M-0018/L-0054 sends REQUEST ADD after successful format negotiation/Handshake Complete. M-0019 places the 30-second submission limit after successful negotiation; L-0055 says after establishing a connection. The connected-state Note and both anchors remain literal, without an invented reconciliation or a 30-second guarantee of successful admission. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller responds with ERROR/ADDED after distinct authentication/authorization conditions within its 30-second limit, and REMOVED under separate deregistration rules; these are not physical equipment transitions.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller responds with ERROR/ADDED after distinct authentication/authorization conditions within its 30-second limit, and REMOVED under separate deregistration rules; these are not physical equipment transitions.

rows.boundary: Required lists two interval properties and seven commands; Recommended lists Identity, Operating State, Clear Property and Set Property. The Note gives implementation forms, not a mandatory transport or permanent actor class.

rows.boundary: CMPT-L-0072–0081 and their explanatory Notes distinguish command enablement from immediate availability, property maintenance/access on request from publication, and observable recording enablement from inclusion in Events. A ready command may still be busy. These states do not establish authorization, execution, an observed physical effect or a measured hardware-health condition. Config false-state-list rules are source-specific message semantics, not invented defaults for every required Boolean. Saved DMS Command/Property/Observable State definitions and their wording notes remain intact. Observation publication includes only ready-and-reporting observables. Command requests are limited to declared commands whose ready state is true, yet a ready command can still be temporarily unavailable, queued or BUSY. Reporting/readiness/request eligibility and immediate execution remain separate. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Service recommendation depends on a received Config declaring the relevant Set ISA ... Service command. Capability declaration, current readiness, provider selection and successful service use remain distinct.

rows.boundary: ICD6.0r5 supports IPL protocol version1 and lists Protocol Buffers/XML long and short forms plus0x05/0x01 Custom Java API encoding. Unsupported/deprecated format pairs and inconsistent printed examples retain their source standing. IPL3 transforms standard capabilities into dedicated declarations/fields/request types while custom content retains generic structures. Neither IPL Format3 nor its schema byte is protocol version3. No actual negotiation,schema-file validation or current security result is asserted. CMPT-L-0042/0043 requires all supported ICD formats in preference order; it adds no Controller selection rule. L-0048 requires the smallest suitable application-data wrapper, while the ICD describes best fit with should. L-0046/0051/0052 require the stated early-data, invalid-type and decode-failure errors. The Sensor CE Format 3 sentence is an explanatory Note, not a universal format mandate. Negotiation completion permits IPL data exchange subject to the later ISA participation restrictions. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller selects a supported IPL format from the sorted offer and reports unsupported formats; the explicit may begin application exchange differs from a mandatory send. Preserve ICD edition boundaries.

The requirements supply no numerical synchronization accuracy, selected deployed clock source, measured clock quality or new DMS clock-status fields. Epoch does not determine timestamp units or collapse occurrence and transmission times; saved UTC/time type definitions retain their own rules.

rows.label: Candidate — Security and accountability audit record
rows.status: AAS O6-1 provisional information-need candidate; NOT ADOPTED
rows.definition: Describe security and accountability audit events, retaining the source-defined event subjects and time basis. Part 4 requires audit records for unauthorized access and identity, account or access-rule configuration changes. When accountability is a concern, information create/update/delete records identify the affected object and reported completion. Audit events identify the acting user application and carry event time to at least seconds. Machine-processable logs are required; exposure as a dedicated Submodel is only an option. No actual audit log, physical action or mandatory DIM event schema is established. C239 separately requires lifecycle/policy/zeroization audit events with UTC when available and uptime otherwise; optional event families, logical collector/relay roles and absent actor/object details remain donor-qualified. Do not impose the AAS payload or time precision on SOSA.

rows.label: Candidate — Secure-startup trust and authentication dependencies
rows.status: SO-2D provisional information-need candidate; NOT ADOPTED
rows.definition: Describe the trust basis and authentication dependencies governing the specialized system start-up sequence: hardware authentication, authenticated runtime/software loading and composition. A Root of Trust may be hardware or software, with cryptographic or design-based trust. SO2_source_correspondence.native_meaning: Describe an equipment declaration about recovery after host power cycling, retaining the triggering condition, the intended return state and whether physical operator intervention is required. SO2_source_correspondence.reason_for_separate_candidate: Generic capability catalogues, mandatory-support lists and readiness reports do not express the trigger-to-recovery behavior or intervention condition. Requested initialization is an action interface; a persistent action flag concerns resuming its associated action; secure startup concerns authentication prerequisites. None states automatic return to communication after a host power cycle.
SO2_source_correspondence.relation: PARTIAL / ADDITIONAL SOURCE-QUALIFIED INFORMATION NEED; no automatic equivalence or adoption
SO2_source_correspondence.classification_rationale: A declaration of the triggering interruption, intended recovery state and required operator intervention is useful across different sensing systems. The source SHALL applies specifically to Class5 and does not become a universal equipment requirement.
SO2_source_correspondence.source_contact: Original C239 Edition1.1 inline/table text reconsulted for the new meaning; retained source findings and original record hashes verified. Figure pixels, full modality matrices and external-native standards not fully audited.
SO2_source_correspondence.source_limits: Native standing is a SHALL for Class5 with Demonstration verification, not proof that any actual device met it. No recovery time, retry/backoff policy, retained-state guarantee, fault coverage or actual successful communication is inferred.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Sensor contributes a specific sensor-system boundary and modality to the proposed described sensing arrangement.
individual_correspondences.guard: Does not prove generic CSAPI System identity, ownership of deployed sensors or a mandatory domain superclass.

individual_correspondences.why: Source's generic System/SubSystem concept permits hierarchical systems without fixing one sensing domain root.
individual_correspondences.guard: Generic SOSA System is not always an instantiated physical sensing apparatus.

individual_correspondences.why: A SOSA Hardware Element is physical and can be a sensor constituent, with source-defined configuration bounds.
individual_correspondences.guard: Not every physical environmental probe or other equipment is a SOSA hardware element.

individual_correspondences.why: PIC, aperture, chassis/enclosure and power supply are documented SOSA hardware/infrastructure examples.
individual_correspondences.guard: SOSA hardware architecture is not universal sensor hardware inventory or mandatory chassis hierarchy.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Host Platform contributes concrete physical support/mounting context for a SOSA Sensor.
individual_correspondences.guard: Does not establish source-specific geolocation, site operator, sensor's own geometry or a software host.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Sensor Pod is an integral packaging and mounting case where sensor and pod boundaries overlap.
individual_correspondences.guard: Cannot always treat pod as external hosting platform or as a physically separate sensor.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA External Interface crosses sensor boundary and may connect to host/environment.
individual_correspondences.guard: Not equivalent to a distinct externally cabled ClimaVue, SDI-12 connector, or all connected equipment.

individual_correspondences.why: Internal interfaces and drawn physical relationships provide relation/context evidence.
individual_correspondences.guard: Interface presence does not entail strict part-of, one function per card or installed topology.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Module is a separately defined functional architecture role that might be implemented on physical hardware.
individual_correspondences.guard: It must NOT be read as physical constituent by label or produce phantom hardware/part-of edges.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Sensor Component and generic Element can include logical/software as well as physical realizations.
individual_correspondences.guard: Cannot silently equate 'component' with physical module, installed probe or hardware individual.

individual_correspondences.why: RTE describes execution hosting of software, not a physical vehicle/structure.
individual_correspondences.guard: Do not use unqualified platform/host terms to infer location or physical attachment.

individual_correspondences.why: Interaction infrastructure carries logical information exchange between modules.
individual_correspondences.guard: Transport/binding cannot prove a distinct network-visible node, physical cable or original measurement author.

individual_correspondences.why: A procurable unit may implement multiple modules/physical infrastructure elements.
individual_correspondences.guard: Purchase unit or product type is not identical to one module, one model designation, one installed asset or one sensor.

individual_correspondences.why: Source's unqualified 'Platform' can describe sensor device, physical host or computing infrastructure.
individual_correspondences.guard: Only qualified 'SOSA Host Platform' has defensible physical host interpretation.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA function/interface decomposition is not ISA CIC visible/opaque member exposure.
individual_correspondences.guard: Do not import ISA network member/virtual UCI semantics into SOSA without exact SOSA source evidence.

individual_correspondences.why: System Manager is a defined management module with subfunctions that can qualify generic role/service concepts
individual_correspondences.guard: SOSA managing module is not ISA Controller service role or one-to-one physical component

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA external mission task request and internal assignment resemble issued action request patterns
individual_correspondences.guard: Task Manager interactions are preliminary; no proven user request or physical effect and no exact CSAPI Command mapping

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA task/assignment status and health reporting potentially qualify reported outcome concepts
individual_correspondences.guard: Published status and return codes not independent completed command or mission success

individual_correspondences.why: Native SOSA Capability depends upon as-configured health and tasks/assignments, unlike ISA CCD static declarations
individual_correspondences.guard: No assertion of equal actual mode/capability list or vendor hardware execution

individual_correspondences.why: Finite SOSA Mode concept speaks to known behavior in a discrete mode
individual_correspondences.guard: Do not equate mode to default or current source-reported mode without evidence

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA mode and status message categories can contribute source-specific mode reporting notions
individual_correspondences.guard: Does not establish actual contemporaneous source-reported mode in one of four cases

individual_correspondences.why: Sensor lifecycle/state is explicit separately from condition and health
individual_correspondences.guard: Do not equate SOSA state enum to ISA operating condition property

individual_correspondences.why: Health diagnostics include BIT execution/results and fault reporting
individual_correspondences.guard: No exact native ISA BIT property or actual device diagnostic measurement

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA reports status/health events but ISO-coded property Status report is a distinct message form
individual_correspondences.guard: Syslog notification is not an ISA Status property-value message

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA manager/agent may represent/manage a different component, similar to mediated participation
individual_correspondences.guard: No exact ISA CIC performer/broker/relay semantics, source exposure or virtual UCI mapping

individual_correspondences.why: In-band management interface roles are networked conditional roles
individual_correspondences.guard: SOSA client/server/agent role is not a unique ISA registered network participant

individual_correspondences.why: Distinct notifications about state/status/fault/mode/configuration supply management change evidence
individual_correspondences.guard: Not equal to ISA Administrative event codes, original Observation or all messages actually delivered

individual_correspondences.why: Manager-represented lifecycle at whole sensor and module/PIC level qualifies possible state context
individual_correspondences.guard: State is not source-reported operating mode or proof observed live condition

individual_correspondences.why: PIC/module Lost Communication provides bounded example of diagnostic/availability ambiguity
individual_correspondences.guard: Loss of management path must not be treated as physical sensor health or measured actual failure

individual_correspondences.why: Task assignment statuses offer some reported processing/execution context
individual_correspondences.guard: Not exact ISA current command execution record or verified hardware effect

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA functional modules can process sensory data but are not necessarily the physical observer
individual_correspondences.guard: Functional chain, data ingestor and physical sensing actor must remain separate

individual_correspondences.why: Data product formatting and storage distinguish output stream/report fields and their provenance
individual_correspondences.guard: No exact CSAPI resultSchema, actual Observation or original-to-digital-copy chain

individual_correspondences.why: Security operational state/integrity and alerts may relate to tamper/health concepts
individual_correspondences.guard: Software integrity result/security state does not prove physical tamper condition

individual_correspondences.why: Calibration module describes reference test signal injection separate from recurring observation procedures
individual_correspondences.guard: No actual metrological calibration performed or reusable ObservingProcedure identity

individual_correspondences.why: Host platform interface/nav/time supply site/host-related operational context
individual_correspondences.guard: Time/nav source is not surveyed position of individual instrument or installation history

individual_correspondences.why: Source describes host power flow and functional power conversion/protection distinctions relevant to original case power hold
individual_correspondences.guard: Module reference only: no installed battery, exact voltage, state, control or actual power telemetry

individual_correspondences.why: Possible power status/reference module supports concept of component power condition
individual_correspondences.guard: Does not establish actual ISA Power State property equivalence or real source-state measurement

individual_correspondences.why: Network monitoring and QoS roles are pertinent to connection/reporting-path distinctions
individual_correspondences.guard: No real source-specific radio transmission, timing, CSAPI transfer or network health proof

individual_correspondences.why: Managed capabilities and manager-reported state need separate readiness interpretation
individual_correspondences.guard: A supported functionality is neither a source-attested current ready flag nor a reported actual state

individual_correspondences.why: Preliminary task model contrasts request/state/status/health and actual implementation
individual_correspondences.guard: No source case has authenticated issued, acknowledged, completed, physically verified command sequence

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA DIV-1 mission/management conceptual scope may help categorize output and management fields
individual_correspondences.guard: SOSA DIV-1 is a model layer, not output-field specification or native CSAPI result schema

individual_correspondences.why: Logical quantities and physical format concepts may inform typed measured data
individual_correspondences.guard: Narrative alone cannot establish a native SOSA measurement type/units, actual value or cardinality

individual_correspondences.why: Physical DSDM encoding pointer is related to datatype specification scope
individual_correspondences.guard: Cannot infer DSDM type list from prose or equate to ISA CCD type declarations

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA RTE software profile/configuration has documented fields
individual_correspondences.guard: It is not native ISA Config message, component capability declaration, runtime configuration of all sensors

individual_correspondences.why: Multiple execution environments/implementations illustrate physical vs logical distinctions
individual_correspondences.guard: No physical containment or one module per PIC, sensor or hardware component

individual_correspondences.why: Request-response interactions describe a request to act or get/set operation
individual_correspondences.guard: Not evidence of a source-attested issued command/physical effect

individual_correspondences.why: Response exists as an interaction type after request
